7.need-data: This stage uses your data and stages 1 to 6: load it and complete them first.

inherit.title: What it inherits from your stages
inherit.no-columns: Stage 4 left no column in use: without columns there's no model.
inherit.scheme: Sealed split (stage 6): {esquema}, with {n} training rows. The test set doesn't enter this stage.
inherit.baseline: Baseline (stage 5): in each fold, whichever costs least on its training rows; your current rule competes if you wrote one.

folds.title: The folds, inside the training rows
folds.none: Two folds can't be built because {razon}.

reason.pocos-casos: a class has very few cases

folds.time-note: By time, each fold validates one period and trains only on what came before, minus the gap of your horizon; the first period only teaches.

verify.title: Checked on your table
verify.rows: No row trains and validates in the same fold.
verify.units: No unit has rows on both sides of a fold.
verify.time: No training row is within a horizon of its validation.
verify.test: No test row enters a fold.
verify.rows-bad: {n} rows train and validate in the same fold.
verify.units-bad: {n} units have rows on both sides of a fold.
verify.time-bad: {n} training rows are within a horizon of their validation.
verify.test-bad: {n} rows that aren't training rows entered a fold.

run.loading: Getting Python ready in your browser…
run.cancelled: You cancelled the run; nothing was recorded.
run.error: The league couldn't run ({motivo}); nothing was recorded.
run.note: It runs in your browser: your data doesn't travel to any server. With many rows it can take a few minutes.

league.title: The league
league.caption: {metrica} in cross-validation: selection measure
league.note: Selection measure: it's the score used to choose, and it's optimistic, because the winner won on exactly these folds. The unbiased measure is the test set, which stage 8 opens once.

why.title: Why it won
why.same: {ganador} had the best selection score ({puntaje}, in cross-validation: good for choosing, not for believing), and there's no simpler model within one standard error ({ee}).
why.simpler: The best selection score was {mejor}'s ({puntaje}, in cross-validation: good for choosing, not for believing). {ganador} came within one standard error ({ee}) and is simpler: a difference smaller than the noise across folds doesn't justify something more complicated.

compare.title: Against what you already get without a model
compare.caption: Cost per 100 decisions, on each fold's validation rows
compare.diff: Baseline minus winner, per 100 decisions: {media} on average (95% interval: {bajo} to {alto}).
compare.supera: It beats the baseline: the whole interval is above zero.
compare.no-supera: It doesn't beat the baseline: the interval touches or crosses zero. That's written down, and stage 8 will measure both on the test set.
compare.note: The folds share training rows: the interval is optimistic and, with few folds, wide.

perm.title: Signal or just chance?
perm.result: With the labels shuffled {n} times, {m} did as well as or better than the winner: p = {p}.
perm.resolution: With {n} permutations, the smallest possible p is {res}.
perm.senal: There's signal: almost no shuffle did as well or better (p ≤ 0.05, a convention).
perm.sin-senal: No clear signal: with random labels the same is reached often; what it found may be chance.
perm.failed: {n} permutations couldn't be scored and don't count.

check.solape_filas: Rows on both sides of a fold
check.solape_unidades: Units on both sides of a fold
check.validacion_antes: Training within a horizon of its validation
check.fuera_entrenamiento: Rows outside the training set in a fold
check.base_costo: Baseline cost per decision, per fold
check.ganador_costo: Winner's cost per decision, per fold
check.perm_mejores: Permutations as good as or better than the winner
